description: The plot illustrates the performance on Qwen2.5, showing the relationship between the co-occurrence number and accuracy percentage. The x-axis is labeled "Co-occurrence Number" with a logarithmic scale, ranging from 0 to 10^3, and tick labels at 10^0, 10^1, 10^2, and 10^3. The y-axis is labeled "ACC (%)" with a linear scale, ranging from 60 to 80, and tick labels at 60, 65, 70, 75, and 80. The plot contains six lines, each representing a different editing method: Base (black, circle marker, solid line), FT (blue, square marker, solid line), IKE (red, triangle marker, solid line), MEND (brown, inverted triangle marker, solid line), MEMIT (purple, diamond marker, solid line), and ROME (green, star marker, solid line). The lines generally increase as the co-occurrence number increases, with the Base line starting at around 67% and ending at around 70%, the FT line starting at around 68% and ending at around 72%, the IKE line starting at around 71% and ending at around 75%, the MEND line starting at around 72% and ending at around 76%, the MEMIT line starting at around 73% and ending at around 77%, and the ROME line starting at around 74% and ending at around 78%.
